svg.title: Task execution pipeline
svg.desc: Every surface but a workflow step ends in TaskService.create, which writes a queued row. TaskExecutor polls queued rows every two seconds: it prepares the project and session, resolves provider and policy, acquires an execution lease, and checks the task out to running. The work then runs unawaited as _executeCore, settles, and releases the lease in a finally block; every failure goes through TaskFailureHandler.

g.text: Hover a box for what it does and how it fails; its connections light up. Click it to open its section.
Inside a rendered document this image is static. Click it to open the interactive SVG.

svg.text: Creation never executes inline. One poll dispatches each queued task onto a lease; the work then runs unawaited.

g.text: POLL · EVERY 2 s · QUEUED TASKS, OLDEST FIRST
Web UI, HTTP API, task_create tool,
Creation surfaces · the UI and API validate the body through TaskCreationService before TaskService.create; schedules call it directly
A workflow step bypasses TaskService: workflow_task_factory inserts execution, task and step rows in one transaction (ADR-023).
TaskService.create · creates or links the AgentExecution in the same transaction as the task row, then records the statusChanged event
A nested transaction is rejected with NestedTransactionError; TaskStatusChangedEvent fires only after the event insert succeeded.
(standalone); the row waits as status = queued
tasks table · persistent task rows behind TaskRepository; the executor is the only reader that turns queued rows into work
Every update is a compare-and-set on status and version, so two actors cannot both move the same row.
poll · one pass of _pollOnceInner: rows from retired task types (research, coding without a worktree declaration) fail here, non-retryably
workflowOnly (zero-server runs) polls workflow-owned tasks only; stop() cancels the timer and active tasks, then drains.
prepare · _prepareQueuedTask then _prepareExecutionSession: an unknown or error project fails the task, a cloning project leaves it queued
The session is SessionKey.taskSession(taskId:) or _continueSessionId; a missing or archived continued session fails the task, non-retryably.
resolve · provider: the task's, else agent.provider, else the primary runner's; resolveForTask picks location and profile
A policy refusal fails the task, non-retryably; no provider leaves it queued and records one taskError event.
acquire · acquire takes a worker-lane permit first, then admits: daily budget, session lock, loop pre-check, rate window
null lease: stays queued. BusyTurnException: later tasks skip acquire this pass. LoopDetected and BudgetExhausted: non-retryable failure.
checkout · TaskService.transition(running, trigger: system), a compare-and-set on status and version
A StateError means another actor moved the task first: the lease is released and the task is skipped for this pass.
prompt, then one turn on the
_executeCore · project and base ref, worktree, execution directory, preconditions, pre-turn budget check, prompt, then the turn
Workflow-owned tasks run WorkflowOneShotRunner on the same lease and record no tokenUpdate or toolCalled events and no trace.
settle · a completed turn collects artifacts, checks the post-turn token budget, transitions per reviewMode, and may call onAutoAccept
A read-only task that mutated its checkout fails here, non-retryably; a cancelled task is skipped.
lease.release() · ExecutionLease.release is idempotent and runs on every path, including a lost checkout race
Reuse, disposal and quarantine are the coordinator's decision; task code never touches the worker cache.
TaskFailureHandler · a retryable failure re-queues the task (running → failed → queued); the next poll restarts at step 1
A repeated failure kind, an exhausted retryCount or a non-retryable site fails it permanently with errorSummary and a taskError event.
